acme_dev: Hey team — we started seeing truncated streaming responses after our users' clients reconnect. The last object (finish_reason) is missing and JSON is left open. Happening on Chrome + mobile webview.

jess_support: Sorry you're hitting this, can you paste a minimal repro and the request headers?

acme_dev: Repro steps: 1) Start a streaming request to /v1/generate with SSE. 2) Kill network (simulate flaky mobile). 3) Reconnect the tab quickly. 4) Client receives an incomplete JSON tail. POST payload below.

acme_dev: ```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Accept: text/event-stream
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "redwood-latest",
  "input": "stream test",
  "stream": true
}
```

acme_dev: Minimal client (node-fetch) we used: ```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const res = await fetch(url, {headers});
res.body.on('data', c => console.log(c.toString()));
```

fred_eng: Do you see a RST or any proxy logs? Any finish_reason at all?

acme_dev: No finish_reason field. The stream just ends with: `... \n}\n,` (trailing comma) or sometimes an open brace. Pretty clearly truncated.

jess_support: Thanks. We had a related incident where a keepalive-on-reconnect from a CDN caused the server to close without flushing the final chunk. Can you share the time range and request id (if present)?

acme_dev: Sure, I have one: request-id: req_9a2f4c, time ~2025-11-08T14:12:04Z. Also saw `connection: keep-alive` on client side.

mike_ops: @fred_eng I pulled the edge logs for req_9a2f4c. I see the backend sent the final SSE event but the edge closed the TCP stream during reestablish. Snippet: `FIN from client during upstream write` then `upstream write error`.

fred_eng: That matches a bug we've been chasing: if the client rapidly reconnects and the edge attempts a keepalive probe, the final chunk can be dropped when the connection transitions states. We've got a PR to add a short drain window to ensure final frames are flushed.

acme_dev: Anything we can do on our side to mitigate right away? Some users are in the middle of grading flows so data loss is bad.

jess_support: Short-term: add a small client-side resume/retry to request the missing finalization. For SSE, you can detect an unterminated JSON and then re-request the last N tokens using the model + prompt + partial output. Example heuristic: if stream ends and last char is not `}` or `]`, call a non-streaming /complete endpoint with the same prompt + context id.

acme_dev: Is there a safer server-side config we can toggle in the meantime?

mike_ops: We can enable a per-route grace-drain flag for your customer route so the edge waits 250ms after upstream EOF before closing client socket. That reduces the chance of an in-flight final chunk being lost. Would you like us to enable for your workspace?

acme_dev: Please enable it. Also would love a stable repro so we can test client-side fallback.

jess_support: Done — I enabled grace-drain on the route for your workspace (req quota unaffected). Can you try reproducing and paste new logs if it still fails?

acme_dev: Testing now... so far I retried 20 times and didn't hit the truncation. Will run against real users tomorrow. Thanks.

fred_eng: Long-term fix: we'll land the drain-window patch and add explicit final-frame ack from the edge to reduce silent EOFs. We'll also add an optional server-sent `finish_reason` heartbeat before connection close so clients can detect expected termination.

acme_dev: One more data point — our mobile webview keeps connections idle for >10s and then reconnects. Could idle keepalive settings be related?

mike_ops: Yes, idle timeouts can cause probes that race with the final flush. We'll drop keepalive probe interval for mobile routes as well as part of the rollout.

jess_support: For tracking: I've created internal ticket SS-1987 and linked req_9a2f4c. We'll update here when the patch is deployed. :spiral_note_pad:

deploy-bot: Deployment started: edge-drain-patch -> canary (fred_eng). build: bld_4821

fred_eng: Canary passed on 5% nodes with no truncation seen in synthetic tests. Rolling to 100% tonight.

acme_dev: Thanks everyone — will reopen if we see further truncated outputs. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
